newsitem.title: USA: Estee Lauder shares dip. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Estee Lauder shares dip. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]

text.p: Estee Lauder Cos Inc shares dipped on Tuesday after the company posted first-quarter numbers that reflected slightly weaker sales in the United States than analysts expected but met consensus per share estimates.
(Corrects headline and first paragraph to clarify that sales were lower than expected, not lower in fact.)
"This was fully in line with our expectations," said Amy Low, an analyst at Goldman Sachs. "I don't have any cause for concern."
Michael Grant, an analyst at J.P. Morgan, said the stock's modest decline was nothing more than "initial reaction to slightly lower U.S. sales" than expected.
The cosmetics company fell 3/4 to 43-3/4 by midday in light volume.
Estee Lauder reported first-quarter earnings of $0.39 per share, matching the First Call consensus estimate, compared to $0.35 per share last year.
Net sales for the quarter were $872.8 million compared with $833.1 million. U.S. sales totaled $507.2 million, a four percent increase over last year.
Leonard Lauder, chairman and chief executive, said in the company's release that the quarterly earnings kept the company on track to meet its objectives for the year.

"With our solid start in the first quarter and our plans for new product launches, geographic expansion, and continued operational efficiencies, we are well-positioned to meet our financial objectives for the fiscal year," he said.
The First Call consensus estimate for the year is $1.40 per share compared with $1.17 per share last year.
Low said she expected to the company to pick up momentum in the second quarter and then take off in the second half of the fiscal year.
